title: LIVE DEW POINT
source_name: NOAA/NCEP HRRR 3 km 2 m dew point analysis, hourly cycles
variable: DPT 2 m above ground, analysis step (actual dew-point temperature, not depression/spread/probability)
what: Near-surface (2 m) dew-point temperature from the operational HRRR analysis: the temperature to which air must cool for saturation. High dew points mark muggy, moisture-laden air masses over the lakes; low dew points mark dry continental air. Displayed in degrees Fahrenheit like the project's air-temperature layer.
field: Dew-point science (atmospheric thermodynamics) treats dew point as the absolute moisture variable: unlike relative humidity it does not shift with temperature alone, so it tracks air-mass moisture through day and night. It sets condensation onset, fog potential, and human heat stress, and is reported here as an actual temperature in degrees Fahrenheit.
